playbook:
When asked to declare my yield, if my sole objective is to maximize my personal points and there is no external incentive to contribute, I declare the minimum allowed (1).

When asked to declare my yield because I want to credibly enable mutual contributions (e.g., to encourage the opponent to deposit or to meet a negotiated collective deal), I declare honestly only if I am willing to follow through by depositing enough to make that signal credible.

When asked to declare my yield and I am behind, I will not declare a high value purely as rhetoric; if I declare high to create room for deposits, I must plan to deposit a substantive portion of that declared amount (sufficient to meaningfully reduce the deficit) — otherwise the high declaration is wasted and may erode credibility.

When put into the deposit step and my goal is to maximize personal points in isolation, I deposit 0 (retain everything for 2 points per unit), because retained gold yields strictly more points per unit than deposited gold.

When put into the deposit step and there is an explicit external payoff, enforceable agreement, or a strategic equilibrium where others will deposit only if I deposit (and the expected returned benefit exceeds the 1-point-per-unit opportunity cost), I deposit the agreed/strategic amount but never more than I declared.

I never deposit more than I declared (the auditor prohibits it), and I do not misdeclare unless the resulting declared/deposited plan is credible and executable without risking audit penalties.

When considering deviating from the default low-declare / zero-deposit play, I require a clear marginal benefit calculation: the expected benefit from inducing others to deposit or from an external reward must exceed the 1-point-per-unit lost by depositing instead of retaining.

I treat temporary high-declare + deposit moves as explicit catch-up gambits: specify target deposit amount, compare expected point swing (including opponent reactions) to simply retaining; only execute if expected net points improve.

I update beliefs about opponents based on observed history: if opponents consistently declare honestly but deposit nothing, I should not expect reciprocation from them and should not sacrifice private points to subsidize the public pot.

I recognize that honest declarations without matching deposits did not improve my score in the observed plays; honesty as a signal must be paired with action to change opponent behavior.

I avoid empty signals: do not declare high unless I will deposit enough to demonstrate commitment; otherwise declare low and keep resources.

1.text:
When I am asked to declare, I declare a number that is at least as large as the amount I intend to deposit this round.

When I have no strategic reason to induce reciprocity, I declare my true private yield (honest declaration). The rounds I played support honesty as a safe default.

When I want to signal cooperation strategically, I may declare a higher number than my private yield—but only if I will not accidentally deposit more than that declared number.

When the deposit decision is put to me, my default action is deposit 0 (retain all gold) because retained gold scores 2 points/unit vs deposit 1 point/unit; the episodes reinforce this as the best baseline when opponents do not reciprocate.

Deposit a positive amount only if the expected reciprocal increase in others’ deposits (translated into my expected points) exceeds the 1-point-per-unit opportunity cost of not retaining. Be explicit: only deposit if E[gain from others per unit I deposit] > 1.

Never deposit more than my declared amount; if there is any risk I might exceed the declared amount, reduce the intended deposit or raise the declaration to avoid an audit failure and the −10 penalty.

If I plan to build a reputation for future rounds in repeated play, consider depositing a small, safe amount (e.g., 1 unit) only when I have reliable early evidence of opponent reciprocity. The episodes showed no early reciprocity, so I should not sacrifice points to "test" opponents unless the experiment is cheap and sufficient remaining rounds exist to recoup the cost.

In the final round, prefer deposit 0 unless there is immediate, verifiable reason to expect a one-shot reciprocal benefit that outweighs the 1→2 tradeoff; with no future rounds to leverage reputation, last-round cooperation is unlikely to pay.

Do not rely on low declarations to avoid audits—declaring less than my intended deposit risks audit and a −10 penalty, so always set declaration ≥ intended deposit.

Be cautious about strategic over-declaration: it can signal cooperation but also allows opponents to misread and increases audit risk if I later change my deposit plan; only over-declare when I plan to follow through with a deposit consistent with the signal.

When uncertain about opponents or when the objective is maximizing my own score in a single match, choose honesty in declaration and deposit 0.
